subject: maths
question: A chord of length 42 cm is drawn in a circle having diameter 58 cm. What is the minimum distance of other parallel chord of length 40 cm in the same circle from 42 cm long chord?
solution:
Given:

The diameter of the circle = 58 cm

The length of one chord = 42 cm

The length of another chord = 40 cm

Formula used:

H2 = B2 + P2

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dbd95765af72bef0a300c03a3d8b7ccdb1b68f11b3e4b61d819463e10ede6ab5.png] 

AB and PQ are two chords, and O is the center of the circle.

M is the midpoint of AB and N is the midpoint of PQ

OB = OQ = 29 cm [radius of the circle]

AB = 40 cm and OB = 29

Then,

AM = MB = 40/2 = 20 cm

In ΔMOB

(OB)2 = (OM)2 + (MB)2

⇒ (29)2 = (OM)2 + (20)2

⇒ 841 = (OM)2 + 400

⇒ (OM)2 = (841 – 400)

⇒ (OM)2 = 441

⇒ OM = 21 cm

Now,

PQ = 42 cm and OB = 29

NQ = PN = 42/2 = 21 cm

In ΔONQ

(OQ)2 = (ON)2 + (NQ)2

⇒ (29)2 = (ON)2 + (21)2

⇒ 841 = (ON)2 + 441

⇒ (ON)2 = (841 – 441)

⇒ (ON)2 = 400

⇒ ON = 20 cm

So according to the question.

⇒ 21 - 20 = 1

**∴ The minimum distance between the two chords is 1 cm.**
